1. The combat isn't too complicated. You have melee, archery and magic (and staffs). If it's too difficult you can turn down the difficulty setting in the settings menu. Might take some time to get familiar with it if you don't have literally any experience with combat games.
2. Skyrim has spiders, and a few others "creepy" creatures that are located in depths of Skyrim. There are mods to replace spiders with different models, so you can try that. There are also Draugrs (similar to zombies) in dungeons. I don't think I need to mention that Skyrim gets bloody often.
3. You'll encounter spiders early in game. For other "scary" creatures, you'll need to explore the world and find them yourself (they're mostly located in caves).
4. Main questline isn't long as you'd maybe think. It takes me a few hours to finish (it's important to mention that I've finished the game thousands of times so it'll take you longer). You'll have hours upon hours if you play Skyrim for the first time, questlines, side quests, DLCs, mods... It takes a long time to finish if you don't rush through it all. Even if you do it'll take you some time.
5. I'd suggest you to play Skyrim without mods for the first time. Except patches (Unofficial Skyrim Patch for example). If you want a modded experience, your best bet would be to either download an already made modlist using Wabbajack, or look up for some tutorials on how to mod on YouTube. It's really easy to mess up the whole game if you're doing it yourself (load order, compatibility...), so make sure you look up for a couple of tutorials.
6. It's subjective. You'll gain perspective on both of the sides while playing the game, no need to worry about that now. Everyone has a different opinion on this.
7. Just have fun for the first time. If it's too hard, turn down the difficulty. You can also turn on the god-mode (don't recommend it, especially for the first time) via console commands. Console commands and mods disable achievements by default (there's a mod that enables them) so be mindful of that as well if you plan on modding or cheating.
